# Filing pull requests and issues

<!-- Generated by components/pr-convention-policy/contract-docs.mjs from components/pr-convention-policy/policy.json and components/issue-body-contract/contract.json in melodic-software/standards. Edit those, run `node components/pr-convention-policy/contract-docs.mjs write`, and commit the result. -->

What a pull request and an issue in an organization repository must carry, for any agent or person
writing one, whatever tool, harness or model writes it. The rules are generated from the two
records that the gates and forms read:
[`policy.json`](https://github.com/melodic-software/standards/blob/main/components/pr-convention-policy/policy.json) for pull requests
and [`contract.json`](https://github.com/melodic-software/standards/blob/main/components/issue-body-contract/contract.json) for issues.
How labels, fields and triage work is the
[issue-tracker playbook](https://github.com/melodic-software/standards/blob/main/standards/process/issue-tracker.md)'s.

## Pull request title

Conventional Commits: `<type>[(<scope>)]: <subject>`, with `!` before the colon for a breaking
change. The type is one of `build`, `chore`, `ci`, `docs`, `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `revert`, `security`, `style`, `test`. A scope is optional. The
`check-contract` step inside the required `CI Status` check fails any other title, and fails a
pull request that carries the `do-not-merge` label.

## Pull request body

Open the body with one linkage line, written as plain text, never in backticks (the gate ignores
code spans):

- `Closes #<issue>` (or `Fixes` or `Resolves`) closes the issue on merge. Use one keyword
  per issue; across repositories, `Closes <owner>/<repo>#<issue>`.
- `Refs: #<issue>` links an issue without closing it. Never write a disclaimer such
  as "does not close #12": GitHub closes the issue anyway, and the gate reports it.
- `No related issue: <reason>` when no issue applies. The reason is required.

Then fill these sections, as `## <name>` headings in this order, each with real content. Their
guidance is the org PR template's:

### Summary

What changes and why, in a sentence or two of problem context.

### Fix

The concrete change and how it addresses the problem.

### Verification

How this was proven: the commands run and what they showed, or the manual check performed.

### Related

Issues, PRs, or decision records this change touches without closing (one per line, e.g. `Refs: #<issue-number>`). This section must not be empty: if nothing applies, say so in a sentence. The no-issue escape goes on the top line of this template, not here.

The body contract is advisory: a miss draws a comment and the `needs-issue-linkage` label instead
of a failed check, but it is expected. Draft from the repository's PR template, else the
`melodic-software/.github` default; `gh pr create --body` skips the template.

## Issues

Title an issue as a plain summary, starting with a verb when it is work to do, with no `X:` or
`[X]` prefix. Set the Issue Type at filing: `gh issue create --type <Type>`.

| Kind | `gh issue create` | Issue form |
|---|---|---|
| Bug Report | `--type Bug` | `bug-report.yml` |
| Feature Request | `--type Feature` | `feature-request.yml` |
| Task | `--type Task` | `task.yml` |
| Agent-Ready Work Item | no `--type`: triage sets it | `agent-ready.yml` |
| Decomposed work item | set by its publisher | none |

A new issue opens with the floor label `needs-triage`: a form applies it, and the floor workflow adds it
to an issue filed without a triage-status label. Never apply a role label such as `agent-ready`
at filing; triage grants it.

Write each field as a heading (`## <heading>` or `### <heading>`) followed by its answer. A required heading
is never left empty or answered `_No response_`.

### Bug Report

Report an unexpected problem or behavior. Form: `bug-report.yml`.

- `Steps to reproduce` (required): Minimal steps that reproduce the behavior.
- `Expected behavior` (required): What should happen?
- `Actual behavior` (required): What actually happens? Include error messages, stack traces, or screenshots.
- `Severity` (required): How bad is it? Say why under Severity justification.
- `Severity justification` (required): One sentence: the blast radius, what it blocks, or the data at risk.
- `Suggested fix location` (optional): The file and function or class where the fix likely belongs, if known. No patch.
- `Environment` (optional): OS, runtime and tool versions, and anything else relevant.

### Feature Request

Propose a new feature or enhancement. Form: `feature-request.yml`.

- `User story` (required): Who benefits and why?
- `Acceptance criteria` (required): How do we know this is done? One verifiable check per line.
- `Affected area / component` (optional): Which part of the project would this affect?

### Task

A chore, maintenance task, audit, or other housekeeping item. Form: `task.yml`.

- `Context` (required): What surfaced this, and what leaving it costs.
- `Proposed work` (required): The concrete next actions.
- `Acceptance criteria` (required): One verifiable check per line.
- `References` (optional): Rules, files, pull requests, or docs this relates to.

### Agent-Ready Work Item

Work written as an agent brief. Triage decides its type and whether it is agent-ready. Form: `agent-ready.yml`.

- `Summary` (required): The change, in one line.
- `Root cause` (optional): Bugs only: unknown, or known: the cause in one line.
- `Current behavior` (required): What the code does today.
- `Desired behavior` (required): What is true once this lands, edge cases and failure handling included. The end state, not edit instructions.
- `Key interfaces` (optional): The types, signatures, config keys, or observable behaviors that change, named by contract rather than file path or line.
- `Acceptance criteria` (required): Checks that each give a yes or no.
- `Out of scope` (required): The neighboring code and features this change leaves as they are.

### Decomposed work item

A vertical slice /work-items:decompose publishes, born triaged; no public form.

- `Outcome` (required): The one observable change a user gets when this slice merges, end to end.
- `Key interfaces` (required): The design this slice touches, named by contract, or None.
- `Done when` (required): The slice's acceptance criteria, each a check with a pass or fail answer.
- `Out of scope` (required): Adjacent work this slice must not change.

## Routing labels

In repositories the automation lanes serve, three labels take an issue off the unattended path,
and each means one thing ([loop-lane convention](https://github.com/melodic-software/claude-code-plugins/blob/main/docs/contracts/loop-lane/README.md#when-work-stops-for-the-owner)):

- `session-owned`: a local session works the issue itself, so the lanes skip it. Apply it when
  you will do the work in your own session. It says who works the item, not whether a person is
  present.
- `attended`: the owner must be present for a manual step on external state an agent cannot
  safely run or test, such as a DNS change, a new key or secret, or an elevated pass. It asks no
  decision, and only the owner removes it.
- `needs-human`: an owner decision is needed. Never use it for ownership or a manual step.

Otherwise leave the issue to the automation lanes: file it with the fields above and no routing
label, and intake triage takes it from there.
